correctness.rationale: The proof derives disjoint support of \(n-1\) real unit columns via strict Clarkson equality for \(p\ne2\). With only n rows, supports force at most one two-coordinate column, yielding exactly a finite 1-dimensional CW graph. Independent signed injection counting gives V=2^(\(n-1\))n!, degree 2(\(n-1\)) and E=(\(n-1\))V. The even-signed coordinate permutation group acts freely and transitively on vertices; its signed star transpositions are precisely incident edges and generate the group. Connected graph topology gives free \(\pi_1\) rank \(E-V+1\). The four-edge two-coordinate loop maps to a full plane rotation under Euclidean column normalization, hence surjects onto Stiefel \(\pi_1\). The enumerator checked exact graph incidences for \(2\le n\le6\), but universal quantifiers rest on the explicit proof.

originality.rationale: The central 2026 full-text source proves support disjointness and fixed-pattern geometry but not their global gluing. The current result identifies a connected signed type-D Cayley graph with an exact factorial free fundamental-group rank and maps it onto the ambient Stiefel fundamental group. Targeted searches for graph, Lamperti, Stiefel, partial-isometry and injective-word equivalents did not reveal a statement that dominates this precise topological classification. This is a best-knowledge priority judgment; pre-existing terminology and unpublished equivalents remain possible.
residual_risks: The signed-star Cayley graph itself may be known under type-D arrangement/permutation terminology; its identification with the global operator-isometry space is the mathematical focus.
Older matrix-isometry topology under a different name might imply the graph result without sharing its formula; publication priority is not independently certified.
Only abstract-level access was obtained for Brown; no whole-document noncoverage conclusion is drawn from it.

value.rationale: The 2026 reference computes only fixed-support strata and motivates the previously missing global topology. With one spare output coordinate the entire nonlinear isometry space becomes a natural finite graph. Its type-D symmetry and factorial free fundamental-group rank measure topological complexity invisible from individual strata or the small fundamental group of the ordinary Stiefel manifold. The precise homotopy type is the first nontrivial codimension boundary for real Lamperti embeddings, making it a natural structural invariant rather than an arbitrary finite example.
